title: Chicken Dhansak
subtitle: A Parsi-inspired curry of chicken, red lentils, and sweet-sour sauce
excerpt: Chicken thighs and red lentils cook together in a tamarind-spiked sauce that is at once rich and bright. The lentils dissolve into the gravy, giving it body without heaviness.
sourceNotes: Based on Parsi dhansak tradition, adapted for the British curry-house style with red lentils and tamarind.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. The lentils thicken on freezing; add a little water when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Make a large batch and freeze in meal-sized portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day as the lentils continue to absorb the sauce. Reheat gently with a splash of stock.

content.text: Dhansak is a sweet-sour curry with Parsi roots, where lentils cook alongside the meat and collapse into the sauce. Tamarind gives it the sharpness that makes this dish stand out from other chicken curries. Watch the heat once the lentils go in; they catch easily on the bottom.
Heat the ghee in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken pieces and turn to coat in the spiced onion base. Cook for 3 minutes until sealed on the outside.
Add the tinned tomatoes, rinsed lentils, and stock. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring now and then. The lentils should melt into the sauce and the chicken should turn tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste, garam masala, and fenugreek leaves. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt and tamarind balance.
Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.

items.symptom: The lentils are catching on the bottom.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough liquid.
items.fix: Turn the heat to low, add another 100ml of stock, and stir from the bottom.

items.cause: Too much tamarind paste was added.
items.fix: Stir in a small pinch of sugar and a little extra salt to balance the sharpness.

items.symptom: The chicken is stringy and dry.
items.cause: Breast meat was used, or the curry cooked at too high a heat.
items.fix: Use thighs next time. This time, shred the dry pieces and stir them back through the lentil sauce.
